messages:
maria_support: FYI — acme-prod is seeing a large number of 429s during the morning traffic spike. Customer reports ~500 429 responses between 08:02–08:06 UTC. They provided a few request ids: 01FZQWERTY1, 01FZQWERTY2, 01FZQWERTY3. Can infra/runtime take a look? :exclamation:

sam_infra: thanks. can you paste one full 429 response (headers + body) and a curl we can run to repro? also which API key/owner is this under (org key, app key, user key)?

maria_support: pasted below. token is org key: acme-corp-prod (we redacted token). here's one raw response they captured from their retry attempt:

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
x-rate-limit-limit: 60
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1710554400
x-trace-id: 01FZQWERTY1
retry-after: 12

{"error":"Rate limit exceeded","code":429,"request_id":"01FZQWERTY1"}

maria_support: they also sent a small timeline: customer sent ~250 reqs/min during 08:03 which included several client-side retries. they say they deployed a change at 07:59 but unclear if that caused a retry loop.

alex_runtime: headers show per-org limit 60 rps and remaining 0 -> quota exhaustion. 500 429s suggests bursty traffic + retries. can someone pull the rate-limiter traces for x-trace-id 01FZQWERTY1..3 and surrounding timeframe? pinging @irene_sre for traces and limiter logs.

irene_sre: on it. also ask customer to run a curl repro with -v so we capture client->server headers and the full response. share this exact repro with them (redact token before posting):

curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"hello"}'

irene_sre: ask them to attach the raw response including headers (we need x-trace-id, x-rate-limit-* and retry-after). if they can also export a HAR of the failing window that would be ideal.

maria_support: sending repro instructions to customer now. also attaching the small HAR they gave — shows repeated immediate retries without backoff at 08:03:12 -> 08:03:40, bursts up to ~120 rps.

debug-bot: debug bundle created: 01FBUNDLE-171055-ACME for org acme-corp-prod — summary: request-rate=250/min during window, limiter-drops=212, 95p-latency=120ms, node=dedicated-us-west-2-3

sam_infra: limiter logs show a short spike: 08:03:12–08:03:40 window with 120rps sustained for ~28s, policy was per-org 60rps. client retries amplified the failures. action items: (1) get customer's HAR + one curl -v output with x-trace-id (maria) (2) irene: pull limiter traces for 01FZQWERTY1..3 and adjacent ids (3) alex: check runtime deploys around 07:59 for any change to retry behaviour or client backoff guidance.

maria_support: customer agreed to run the curl -v and upload the HAR + a redacted token. they also included a screenshot of headers where retry-after was present but they retried earlier. asked them to include exact X-Client-Request-Id and User-Agent.

irene_sre: pulled limiter trace for 01FZQWERTY1 — shows drop at limiter node 3, reason=burst_exceed, client_ip=52.14.23.7, observed_burst_peak=128rps. saving logs to /internal/sre/171055/01FZQWERTY1.log (internal).

sam_infra: we should offer two mitigations: 1) recommend customer implement exponential backoff with jitter and per-instance local token bucket; 2) provision a temporary burst buffer on dedicated nodes (small soft bump) while customer fixes retry loop. i'll draft the support plan.

maria_support: will coordinate the temporary quota bump if you confirm it's safe. customer asked for a timeline — requesting we aim for a short-term bump in next 2 hours if possible.

irene_sre: final note: include the customer's curl -v output and the x-trace-ids in the support ticket. once we have them we can link limiter traces to request logs and close the loop.

sam_infra: assigned. keeping thread open until we get customer's HAR + one curl repro. :thumbsup:
